findings.title: Flusher processes are not terminated when join timeout expires
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before calling `process.terminate()`. If `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on the first flusher process consumes the entire `timeout`, the loop breaks early and skips calling `process.terminate()` on all remaining alive flusher processes. Those worker processes are left running in the background (for example across consumer partition rebalances), continuing to flush Redis shards and produce duplicate segments alongside newly spawned flusher processes.

findings.title: ZeroDivisionError when consumer is initialized with no assigned partitions
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, if `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty (which happens when a Kafka consumer instance is assigned 0 partitions), `self.num_processes` evaluates to `0`, and `process_index = i % self.num_processes` or a passed `max_processes=0` with non-empty shards raises `ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero`. Even when `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty so the loop does not execute, passing `--flusher-processes 0` with non-empty shards will crash with `ZeroDivisionError` because `max_processes or len(...)` falls back only on falsy values while negative values are not guarded.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` on `wait_produce` timer
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 tag metrics with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 tags `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). This makes the tag key inconsistent across the flusher metrics.
